comment: Estimates in seconds, used only to balance the shards and to order them (longest first). Measured on GitHub runners (ubuntu-24.04, 4 vCPU) in the runs of 2026-11-19, as the 'ok' seconds of `go test` in the shard logs: internal/lint 121, internal/adminapi 422, internal/store 105, internal/app 85, internal/worker/smssend 61, internal/admincli 45, internal/auth/session 34, internal/auth/login 26, and the oracle shards of internal/api 90 to 134 each (api_split is their mean), internal/api without them 555 to 620. internal/store/catalogtest is NOT measured: both runs stopped it early on the Postgres 18.7 catalogue check (61 s), so its 150 is a guess to replace after a green run. The mutant numbers are seconds as if the mutants ran one at a time and are not measured per mutant; with -j 2 a shard of the first runs took 6 to 9 minutes of wall time against estimates near 4600, so the shard timeouts, which are set from the estimate, stay generous on purpose. A wrong value unbalances the shards and breaks nothing.
